## Design

### 2026-10-11 – ## Week 1: Designing my Starbie PCB

**11h**

## Week 1: Designing my Starbie PCB

I started this session as a complete beginner with KiCad, so most of the time went into learning the tools while following the Starbie guide.

**Setup**
- Created a public GitHub repo for the project and linked it to my project page.
- Installed KiCad 10.0.7 and added the Seeed XIAO symbol library and the Imported Parts footprint library from the care package.

**Schematic**
- Placed the XIAO ESP32-C3 and wired power (5V, 3.3V, GND).
- Added two push buttons (BTN1 on D2, BTN2 on D3), the OLED header and the MPU6050 header sharing SDA (D4) and SCL (D5), and the DHT11 on D1.
- Added a 10k pull-up resistor on the DHT11 data line, which I first missed and found by comparing my schematic with the guide.
- Put no-connect flags on the unused XIAO pins. ERC finished with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

**Footprints and PCB**
- Assigned footprints from the guide's table and updated the PCB from the schematic.
- The update showed 8 "pad not found" errors for XIAO pads 15 to 22, which are pins I did not use.
- Arranged the parts, drew the board outline on Edge.Cuts, and routed every connection by hand using both layers.

**Problems I ran into**
- My first power wiring was too close together, so I redid it to keep 3.3V and GND clearly separate.
- DRC found broken SDA and SCL traces where I changed layers. I deleted the loose pieces and rerouted them. Unconnected items went to 0.
- The only DRC errors left are the two J1 courtyard errors that the guide says to ignore.

**Next**
- Fill in the BOM, upload the KiCad files and firmware to the repo (done), and submit. I still need to build the board in Week 6.

### 2026-10-11 – Finished the project files and put together my bill of materials.

**8h**

Finished the project files and put together my bill of materials.

Repo and files
- Fixed the README so the PCB image shows (the file had been uploaded as starbie-pcb.png.png, so the link was broken).
- Uploaded the KiCad project files and Starbie.ino to my GitHub repo. All required repo checks now pass.

Bill of materials
- Searched for every part on Amazon and AliExpress and compared prices.
- Amazon shipping to Nigeria was $12.33 on top of the parts, which would blow the $30 limit, so I looked at AliExpress instead.
- Checked that parts match my PCB footprints: OLED pin order is GND, VCC, SCL, SDA, and the MPU6050 header order matches my schematic.
- Found that one DHT11 listing was a 3-wire module on its own board, which would not fit my footprint, so I looked for the bare 4-pin sensor instead.
- Entered the parts, quantities, vendors and prices in the BOM.
